newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Shuttle Columbia set for launch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Shuttle Columbia set for launch.

text.p: With some last-minute problems resolved, the U.S. space shuttle Columbia was poised for blastoff on a 16-day science mission on Friday.
NASA officials said Columbia, the oldest of the four shuttles, was set to lift off its seaside launch pad at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre at 2 p.m. EST (1900 GMT) on Friday.
The mission had been delayed by 24 hours to fit some missing thermal insulation to the shuttle's cooling system. The launch team also dealt with two other minor technical glitches.
"That's all behind us now," shuttle operations director Bob Sieck told a news conference on Thursday. "We're proceeding with the count."
Loading of the shuttle's giant rust-coloured fuel tank with half a million gallons (1.9 million litres) of supercold rocket fuel was due to get underway at about 5 a.m. EST (1000 GMT).
During the mission, seven astronauts will work around the clock in two shifts inside a European-built laboratory housed in Columbia's cargo bay.
The crew's research programme features studies into the behaviour of fire in zero gravity and the development of new materials.

Medical experiments will include investigations into the structure of proteins related to Chagas' disease, an infectious parasitic disease found only in parts of South and Central America. Named after the Brazilian physician Carlos Chagas, the disease is spread by certain insects and affects 24 million people.
"This could be the first step on an eventual therapy to deal with the debilitating affects of the disease," said Joel Kearns, director of NASA's microgravity office.
U.S. Air Force meteorologists were predicting a 90 percent chance of fair weather for Columbia's afternoon blastoff.
